note: The INVOCATION-PATH contract (W16-16, issue #522). Every capability listed here MUST be reachable from the product by at least one real invocation path — a CLI verb, an HTTP route, a UI button, or a production (non-test) caller in a shipped pipeline/harness. The structural guard integration/tests/test_capability_invocation_paths.py enforces this: for a symbol-kind entry it AST-checks that the named `entry` symbol is really referenced by some production (non-test, non-self) .py file under the product roots; for a cli_verb-kind entry it checks the verb is registered in the named CLI's parser. A capability that becomes orphaned (its only references are its own definition + tests) turns that test RED. The cloud/Kubernetes exploitation CONFIRMATIONS are ALSO enumerated automatically from docs/capability-matrix/evidence-branches.json (any evidence branch whose implementation_refs name a `integration/vigil_integration/live/*_verify.py:<fn>` producer), so a NEW confirmation branch with no caller reddens the test even if it is never added here — this registry is the human-readable twin of that automatic enumeration. `entry` is `path:symbol`; `verb` is `<cli>:<verbname>` where cli is `vigil` or `framework.v2 <group>`. `residual` states any honest external dependency for a FULL live run (the invocation path exists regardless).
